To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
70% of a mobile data traffic can be offloaded to WiFi networks, and the delay in offloading is around 2 hours.

WiFi offloading can achieve an average of 70% of 3G traffic reduction if the user is willing to tolerate a delay of 2 hours in data transfer, and we have developed a tool that allows network providers to obtain an analytical estimate on the average offloading efficiency for a given WiFi deployment scenario.

(i) 70% of 3G traffic can be offloaded if users can tolerate two hour delay in transfer; (ii) the offloading efficiency is highly dependent on the traffic type; (iii) the offloading performance is highly dependent on how users use WiFi, i.e., whether they are in the coverage of WiFi and how long they stay in the coverage; and (iv) we developed a theoretical framework to predict the performance of offloading.
